meta.description: Curated fragrance recommendations from Arielle's scent profile consultations

recommendations.name: Vetiver Fauve
recommendations.notes: vetiver, hay, earth, smoke, leather
recommendations.profileNote: Photorealistic vetiver with dirty-hay animalics — perfectly calibrated for your profile.

recommendations.name: French Lover
recommendations.notes: vetiver, elemi, incense, oakmoss, gaiac wood
recommendations.profileNote: Woody-green incense with real oakmoss bite. Unisex classic that reads like forest floor in the best way.
recommendations.where: La Jetée Nashville; Neiman Marcus; fmparfums.com

recommendations.name: Coven
recommendations.notes: birch tar, smoke, vetiver, leather, mineral
recommendations.profileNote: Birch tar and smoke over cold mineral earth. No sweetness, total darkness. Perfect November fragrance.

recommendations.name: Dryad
recommendations.notes: oakmoss, violet leaf, vetiver, cedar, labdanum
recommendations.profileNote: The forest spirit fragrance — deep oakmoss and violet leaf over resinous base. Rare naturalistic masterwork.

recommendations.name: Irish Leather
recommendations.notes: irish whiskey, leather, peat, cedarwood, vetiver
recommendations.profileNote: Peaty whiskey leather with zero sweetness. Smells like a cold distillery at dusk. Essential dark-season fragrance.

recommendations.name: Hwyl
recommendations.notes: hinoki wood, cryptomeria, vetiver, oakmoss, incense
recommendations.profileNote: Japanese forest in a bottle — hinoki cypress and cryptomeria over vetiver and incense. Deeply meditative.

recommendations.name: Ouranon
recommendations.notes: petrichor, cedar, vetiver, violet leaf, amber
recommendations.profileNote: Petrichor and violet leaf over cedarwood — smells like rain on hot stone. Your mineralic-green bullseye.

recommendations.name: Eremia
recommendations.notes: desert sand, galbanum, cistus, vetiver, labdanum
recommendations.profileNote: Arid desert botanicals — galbanum and cistus over dry vetiver and labdanum. Otherworldly and precise.

recommendations.name: Néroli Outrenoir
recommendations.notes: neroli, petitgrain, violet leaf, white musk, cedar
recommendations.profileNote: Clean neroli with petitgrain and violet leaf — avoids orange blossom indole trap. Bright and photorealistic.

recommendations.name: Wulong Cha X
recommendations.notes: oolong tea, bergamot, cedarwood, vetiver, musk
recommendations.profileNote: Photorealistic oolong tea accord — roasted, green, slightly smoky. Nothing synthetic. Stunning in-genre piece.

recommendations.name: Sycomore
recommendations.notes: vetiver, sandalwood, cypress, juniper, woody notes
recommendations.profileNote: The benchmark smoky vetiver-sandalwood fragrance. Understated and architectural — daily driver potential.

recommendations.name: Interlude Man
recommendations.notes: incense, oregano, birch tar, labdanum, amber
recommendations.profileNote: Massive incense and labdanum with herbal oregano top — the definitive dark-resinous benchmark. Sample mandatory.

recommendations.name: Patchouli 24
recommendations.notes: patchouli, birch tar, vanilla, woody notes, smoke
recommendations.profileNote: Birch tar patchouli with smoky vanilla — polarizing but essential reference point for dark patchouli category.

recommendations.name: Ippuku
recommendations.notes: Japanese green tea, hinoki, cedar, vetiver, earth
recommendations.profileNote: Photorealistic Japanese green tea over hinoki and earth — fills the tea-forward gap in your collection beautifully.

recommendations.name: Boswellia Scotia
recommendations.notes: Scottish frankincense, green resin, birch, cold air, mineral
recommendations.profileNote: Frankincense sourced from Scottish botanicals — cold, green, mineral. Nothing like Middle-Eastern church incense. Unique in world perfumery.

recommendations.name: Firewater
recommendations.notes: Scotch whisky, smoke, peat, leather, earth
recommendations.profileNote: Peated Scotch whisky rendered in parfum — smoky, leathery, earth-forward. Scottish analogue to Irish Leather with more smoke.

recommendations.name: Spell 125
recommendations.notes: musk, earth, skin, ambergris, woods
recommendations.profileNote: Alessandro Gualtieri's skin-and-earth opus — animalic without being literal. Works with your skin's chemistry not against it.

recommendations.name: Tea for Two
recommendations.notes: lapsang souchong, almond, vanilla, cinnamon, smoke
recommendations.profileNote: Smoky lapsang souchong tea with warm spice — the cozy dark tea counterpart to Wulong Cha's precision.

recommendations.name: Grand Beau
recommendations.notes: tuberose, jasmine, rose, musk, amber
recommendations.profileNote: Potentially indolic tuberose — must skin-test given your tuberose/jasmine sensitivity. If it works on you, this is the house's masterpiece.

recommendations.name: Myrrh Shadow
recommendations.notes: myrrh, incense, dark woods, shadow accord, smoke
recommendations.profileNote: Dark myrrh and shadow — deeper and more resinous than Rock the Myrrh, less animalic. Worth comparing directly.

recommendations.name: Voodoo Chile
recommendations.notes: green pepper, vetiver, lime, earth, woods
recommendations.profileNote: Green pepper and vetiver — photorealistic vegetal-green. Offbeat and interesting for your collection's green quadrant.

recommendations.name: Crazy Basil
recommendations.notes: basil, fig leaf, green herbs, white woods, musk
recommendations.profileNote: Basil-forward green herb fragrance — fills the culinary-green gap alongside Ingenious Ginger.

recommendations.name: B683
recommendations.notes: mineral accord, vetiver, white woods, musk, salt
recommendations.profileNote: The house's most mineralic offering — crystalline and cold. Lower indole risk than florals. Pairs beautifully with your coastal notes.

recommendations.name: Fille en Aiguilles
recommendations.notes: pine resin, incense, fir balsam, amber, woods
recommendations.profileNote: Pine resin and fir balsam — the definitive conifer-incense fragrance. More architectural than Hwyl, more resinous than French Lover.

recommendations.name: Ambre Sultan
recommendations.notes: amber, labdanum, oregano, myrtle, coriander
recommendations.profileNote: Herbal-amber with Mediterranean botanicals — warmer and spicier than your typical resinous pieces. Oregano note is stunning.

recommendations.name: Encens Suave
recommendations.notes: frankincense, myrrh, rose, amber, woody notes
recommendations.profileNote: Soft frankincense and myrrh with rose — warmer and more approachable than Boswellia Scotia but equally serious.

recommendations.name: Falcon Leather
recommendations.notes: leather, birch tar, aldehydes, saffron, amber
recommendations.profileNote: Leather and birch tar with saffron — smoky and animalic in the style of Irish Leather but warmer and more precious.

recommendations.name: Hemingway
recommendations.notes: tobacco, leather, rum, oud, amber
recommendations.profileNote: Tobacco-leather with rum and oud — richly masculine in the old literary sense. Strong candidate for your dark rotation.

recommendations.name: Russian Tea
recommendations.notes: black tea, bergamot, leather, smoke, tobacco
recommendations.profileNote: Lapsang-adjacent dark tea with leather and tobacco — if Tea for Two is the cozy version, this is the serious one.

recommendations.name: Ultima Storia
recommendations.notes: oud, leather, rose, saffron, amber
recommendations.profileNote: The house's dark oud-leather opus. Higher rose content than Grand Beau but less indolic risk. Second priority after testing Grand Beau.

recommendations.name: Megamare
recommendations.notes: marine, seaweed, mineral, ambergris, salt
recommendations.profileNote: Alessandro Gualtieri's ocean fragrance — not the synthetic Davidoff Cool Water marine, but actual seaweed and ambergris. Fills your coastal category deeply.

recommendations.name: Bois d'Ascèse
recommendations.notes: birch smoke, vetiver, cedarwood, incense, earth
recommendations.profileNote: Campfire smoke over cedarwood — the definitive wood-smoke fragrance. Nothing sweet, nothing soft.

recommendations.name: Shadow People
recommendations.notes: black musk, vetiver, dark incense, ash, smoke
recommendations.profileNote: Perfume oil cult classic — black musk and vetiver with incense and ash. Affordable entry into dark fragrance oils.

recommendations.name: Hyrax
recommendations.notes: hyraceum (Africa stone), tobacco, leather, wood, dark earth
recommendations.profileNote: Hyraceum-based animalic — unusual, intense, and deeply naturalistic. For days when Orchid Mantis feels too delicate.

recommendations.name: The Noir 29
recommendations.notes: fig, tea, vetiver, cedarwood, musk
recommendations.profileNote: Dark fig and tea accord over vetiver — a deeper, moodier companion to Philosykos in the fig family.

recommendations.name: Santal 33
recommendations.notes: sandalwood, cedar, cardamom, violet, amber
recommendations.profileNote: Cultural touchstone fragrance — over-worn but a genuine quality piece. Good reference for what your collection does better or differently.

recommendations.name: A Midnight Stroll
recommendations.notes: nightshade, mushroom, dark florals, incense, earth
recommendations.profileNote: Nightshade mushroom and dark florals — deeply weird and photorealistic. A rare mycological fragrance that actually smells like a night walk.

recommendations.name: Sova
recommendations.notes: oat, hay, grain, soft woods, amber
recommendations.profileNote: Grain and hay accord — photorealistic farmland-pastoral. Different angle on the green-naturalistic profile than your existing pieces.

recommendations.name: Trimerous
recommendations.notes: iris, violet, vetiver, earth, woody notes
recommendations.profileNote: Iris and vetiver — cold, mineralic, rooty. Fills the futuristic-floral quadrant differently than Flower Glyph.

recommendations.name: The Golden Cattleya
recommendations.notes: orchid, ylang ylang, vanilla, amber, woods
recommendations.profileNote: Orchid and amber — compares interestingly to Orchid Mantis. More wearable, less challenging.

recommendations.name: Chèvrefeuille
recommendations.notes: honeysuckle, green leaves, jasmine, musk, woods
recommendations.profileNote: Honeysuckle rendered naturalistically — green-floral without the typical indolic jasmine support. Softer floral option.

recommendations.name: Vetyverio
recommendations.notes: vetiver, grapefruit, green notes, cedar, musk
recommendations.profileNote: Citrus-bright vetiver — sunny and green rather than smoky. Pairs well with your collection as the daytime vetiver option.

recommendations.name: Of True Minds
recommendations.notes: petrichor, wet slate, cedar, white musk, mineral
recommendations.profileNote: Petrichor and wet slate — the Liis fragrance most aligned with your mineralic-green profile. Highest priority within the Liis catalog.

recommendations.name: Bo
recommendations.notes: fig, green leaves, warm skin, cedar, sandalwood
recommendations.profileNote: Fig and green leaf — lighter and more skin-forward than Philosykos. Worth comparing if the fig category appeals.

recommendations.name: Orpheon
recommendations.notes: juniper berries, cypress, labdanum, cedar, musk
recommendations.profileNote: Juniper and cypress over labdanum — architectural and restrainted. You own this — use as reference for how green-dark should resolve.

recommendations.name: Hacivat
recommendations.notes: bergamot, pink pepper, cedarwood, vetiver, musk
recommendations.profileNote: Bergamot-cedar with vetiver base — polished green-woody. More accessible than most of your collection but genuinely good.

recommendations.name: Jazz Club
recommendations.notes: rum, tobacco, vanilla, vetiver, tonka bean
recommendations.profileNote: Rum-tobacco-vanilla — nostalgic and approachable. Lower niche ambitions but genuinely pleasant for casual wear.

recommendations.name: By the Fireplace
recommendations.notes: chestnut, smoke, clove, guaiac wood, vanilla
recommendations.profileNote: Campfire and chestnuts — sweet-smoky rather than resinous-smoky. Accessible smoke fragrance for comparison against Bois d'Ascèse.

recommendations.name: Misia
recommendations.notes: violet, rose, iris, musk, sandalwood
recommendations.profileNote: Violet and iris — powdery but precise. Reference point for the mineralic-floral style your Flower Glyph operates near.

recommendations.name: Infusion d'Iris
recommendations.notes: iris, cedar, amber, incense, white musk
recommendations.profileNote: Iris and cedar — clean, mineralic, restrained. A more accessible iris reference than Trimerous.

recommendations.name: Oudin
recommendations.notes: oakmoss, leather, hay, labdanum, amber
recommendations.profileNote: Oakmoss leather with hay — a rougher, more animalic cousin to Dryad from the same house.

recommendations.name: Bête Noire
recommendations.notes: black pepper, dark woods, leather, smoke, resin
recommendations.profileNote: Pepper and dark woods — spicy-dark. Worth exploring alongside Firewater to see which smoke direction resonates.

recommendations.name: Laminaria
recommendations.notes: seaweed, marine, mineral, salt, driftwood
recommendations.profileNote: Kelp and seaweed — photorealistic coastal. Compare directly to Megamare to see which marine treatment you prefer.

recommendations.name: Eucalyptus Yuzu
recommendations.notes: eucalyptus, yuzu, green herbs, cedar, musk
recommendations.profileNote: Eucalyptus and yuzu — bright, medicinal-green. Unusual opening that might appeal given your green preference.

recommendations.name: Fuego Futuro
recommendations.notes: smoke, dry woods, resin, dark herbs, ash
recommendations.profileNote: Ash-smoke and dry woods — more atmospheric than Irish Leather, less structured. Lower priority than Grand Beau or Ultima Storia.

recommendations.name: Encens et Buires
recommendations.notes: frankincense, birch tar, leather, rose, woody notes
recommendations.profileNote: Frankincense and birch tar over leather — darker and more ascetic than Encens Suave. Medieval in feel.

recommendations.name: Fleur de Figuier
recommendations.notes: fig flower, green fig, milky sap, woody notes
recommendations.profileNote: Fig flower accord — lighter and more floral than Philosykos, which you own. Interesting comparison within the fig family.

recommendations.name: Jonquille de Nuit
recommendations.notes: jonquil, narcissus, white musk, woods, green notes
recommendations.profileNote: Narcissus-jonquil — cool and slightly green-floral. A more interesting floral than their typical range.

recommendations.name: Navitus Marin
recommendations.notes: sea air, cedar, mineral, vetiver, musk
recommendations.profileNote: Marine-mineral over cedarwood — more restrained coastal fragrance than Megamare but with real quality.

recommendations.name: Tabac Rouge
recommendations.notes: tobacco, rose, dark woods, incense, amber
recommendations.profileNote: Belle Époque tobacco-rose — historical style rather than modern. Interesting if you want to explore old-school dark fragrances.

recommendations.name: Blue Talisman Extrait
recommendations.notes: iris, violet, amber, oud, sandalwood
recommendations.profileNote: Iris and oud extrait — intensely mineralic-futuristic. Very high bar but remarkable if your skin agrees.

recommendations.name: AO (Antagonist Opus)
recommendations.notes: smoke, oak, leather, dark florals, ash
recommendations.profileNote: Pacific Northwest apothecary aesthetic — smoke and oak and dark florals. Very niche but thematically aligned with your sensibility.

recommendations.name: Anubis
recommendations.notes: myrrh, incense, saffron, immortelle, labdanum
recommendations.profileNote: Ancient Egyptian incense accord — myrrh and immortelle over labdanum. Extreme but relevant to your darkest Nov-Feb rotation.

recommendations.name: Lovely Patchouli 55
recommendations.notes: patchouli, amber, bergamot, rose, sandalwood
recommendations.profileNote: Heritage patchouli from the Grace Kelly–era house. Historical rarity and genuine quality — not the hippie patchouli you know.

recommendations.name: Olibanum
recommendations.notes: frankincense, green resin, citrus, mineral, wood
recommendations.profileNote: Pure frankincense study — green and resinous without any church-incense weight. Less accessible than Boswellia Scotia but more extreme.

recommendations.name: Fueguia Patagonia
recommendations.notes: Patagonian botanicals, lenga beech, cold air, earth, wood
recommendations.profileNote: Wild Patagonian landscape accord — cold and austere with real botanicals. Among the most expensive and rare green fragrances made.

recommendations.name: Absolue de Mousse
recommendations.notes: oakmoss, treemoss, myrrh, labdanum
recommendations.profileNote: Myrrh and photorealistic green in one bottle — the house calls it resinous, mossy, bitter-green. Single best fit found in the indie deep dive.

recommendations.name: Mousse Illuminée
recommendations.notes: treemoss, frankincense, green cypress, artemisia, laurel, cedar, white musk
recommendations.profileNote: Frankincense over real treemoss. Incense and green at once, and Cross uses restricted naturals so the moss reads as material not accord.

recommendations.name: Mousse Illuminée Grand Cru
recommendations.notes: treemoss, frankincense, champaca, rose, absinthe
recommendations.profileNote: All-natural 30ml extrait version. Worth comparing against the standard once you know you like the base.

recommendations.name: Targhee Forest
recommendations.notes: pine, moist forest soil, moss, amber
recommendations.profileNote: Pine over wet forest soil — photorealistic damp-woods green at $85.

recommendations.name: Rostracto
recommendations.notes: rose, fir balsam, artemisia, oakmoss, benzoin, charred cedar
recommendations.profileNote: Fir balsam and charred cedar over oakmoss. The smoky end of Rogue's green range.

recommendations.name: Derviche
recommendations.notes: bergamot, labdanum, vanilla, antique jasmine, olibanum, sandalwood, tobacco
recommendations.profileNote: Non-sweet vanilla with olibanum and labdanum. CAUTION: antique jasmine is in it — sample before committing given how jasmine absolute reads on you.

recommendations.name: Holy Cross
recommendations.notes: watercress, common juniper, blue yarrow, mountain bluebell, lodgepole pine, bearded lichen, ambrette seed, wet stone
recommendations.profileNote: Note list reads like a field guide — alpine green plus wet stone. The 2026 release and the clearest photorealistic-green buy on the list.

recommendations.name: Ivymoss
recommendations.notes: climbing ivy, green tea, spearmint, lime rind, lemon verbena, waterlily, emerald cypress, mugo pine, cedarwood, oakmoss, treemoss, cedarmoss
recommendations.profileNote: Green tea inside a heavy moss build, and fresher than that sounds. Currently sold out — Pineward rotates seasonally, so watch for the return.

recommendations.name: Boreal
recommendations.notes: pine needles, mint, cedar, resins, oakmoss
recommendations.profileNote: Cold northern conifer, 31% extrait. Reformulated spring 2026 toward more Virginia cedar.

recommendations.name: Tea Service
recommendations.notes: black tea, in-house tea extract, soft woods
recommendations.profileNote: Sydney house working with real tea extracts rather than tea accords. Seven fragrances total — the tea specialist your profile was missing.
recommendations.where: chasingscents.com — AUD 160 (~$105); travel spray AUD 55; discovery set AUD 75

recommendations.name: Private Teahouse
recommendations.notes: tea, wood, quiet florals
recommendations.profileNote: The interior-and-wood version of their tea work. Safe pick given your flags.
recommendations.where: chasingscents.com — AUD 160 (~$105); travel spray AUD 55; discovery set AUD 75

recommendations.name: Rain Tea
recommendations.notes: tea, petrichor, wet air
recommendations.profileNote: Tea crossed with petrichor — tea and the mineralic-wet register you already like together.
recommendations.where: chasingscents.com — AUD 160 (~$105); travel spray AUD 55; discovery set AUD 75

recommendations.name: Slow World
recommendations.notes: tea, soft woods, musk
recommendations.profileNote: The quietest of the line. Include in the discovery set rather than buying blind.
recommendations.where: chasingscents.com — AUD 160 (~$105); travel spray AUD 55; discovery set AUD 75

recommendations.name: Bitter Melon Lemon Tea
recommendations.notes: bitter melon, lemon, black tea
recommendations.profileNote: Bitter-green citrus tea. The vegetal bitterness is the interesting part, not the lemon.
recommendations.where: chasingscents.com — AUD 160 (~$105); travel spray AUD 55; discovery set AUD 75

recommendations.name: Matcha Break
recommendations.notes: matcha, milk, green tea
recommendations.profileNote: RULED OUT unless you retest matcha. Matcha in a starring role has gone skatolic on you before, and this is a matcha-latte concept.
recommendations.where: chasingscents.com — AUD 160 (~$105); travel spray AUD 55; discovery set AUD 75

recommendations.name: Lapsang Lover
recommendations.notes: lapsang tea tincture, black tea, labdanum, fossilized amber, myrrh, rose, resins, cardamom, honey
recommendations.profileNote: Tea and myrrh in the same bottle, all natural. Colour comes from repeated steepings and black tea distillation. Start with the $46 roller.

recommendations.name: Moss Gown
recommendations.notes: oakmoss, green notes, soft woods
recommendations.profileNote: All-natural oakmoss green. Cheap enough to sample alongside Lapsang Lover.

recommendations.name: Sedona Sweet Grass
recommendations.notes: sweet grass, hay, dry green notes
recommendations.profileNote: Hay and sweet grass — the dry-pastoral end of green, adjacent to Vetiver Fauve's hay facet.

recommendations.name: Voyeur Verde
recommendations.notes: green notes, herbs, woods, musk
recommendations.profileNote: Maya Njie's green entry. Ten fragrances since 2016 — the slowest-releasing house in band.

recommendations.name: Nordic Cedar
recommendations.notes: cedar, dry woods, musk
recommendations.profileNote: Restrained Scandinavian cedar. Quieter than anything in your current rotation.

recommendations.name: Vanilj
recommendations.notes: cardamom, cedarwood, vanilla, patchouli, amber, musk
recommendations.profileNote: Restrained rather than sugary, but it leans powdery and cardamom-bun doughy — not the austere vanilla you are after. Sample before counting it as your non-sweet vanilla.

recommendations.name: Tobak
recommendations.notes: tobacco, dry woods, spice
recommendations.profileNote: Dry tobacco. Worth a sample slot in the £34 discovery set rather than its own purchase.

recommendations.name: Azalai
recommendations.notes: saffron, blood orange, gum acacia, salty amber, incense, mint tea, dried fruit, velvione musk
recommendations.profileNote: Incense and mint tea together, built on salty amber. Stora Skuggan releases about one a year — nine total since 2015.

recommendations.name: Silphium
recommendations.notes: silphium accord, ancient incense, woods, leather
recommendations.profileNote: A reconstruction of an extinct Cyrenian plant set against ancient incense. Conceptually the most interesting thing in the deep dive.

recommendations.name: Pine
recommendations.notes: pine, conifer resin, cold air
recommendations.profileNote: Their 2024 conifer. Compare directly against Pineward Boreal to see whose pine you prefer.

recommendations.name: Incense Extrême
recommendations.notes: frankincense, myrrh, orris, dry woods, spices
recommendations.profileNote: The dry frankincense-and-myrrh benchmark — the reference point your myrrh category needs. Tauer builds on his ambreine base — same class of high-dose amber that has given you headaches, so sample first.
recommendations.where: tauerperfumes.com — CHF 117–205 (~$145–195)/50ml; US retail via Luckyscent, Twisted Lily

recommendations.name: L'Air du Désert Marocain
recommendations.notes: cumin, coriander, petitgrain, cedar, incense, ambergris, vanilla
recommendations.profileNote: The cult dry incense-amber. Arid rather than sweet, and the closest thing to a canonical text in this category. Tauer builds on his ambreine base — same class of high-dose amber that has given you headaches, so sample first.
recommendations.where: tauerperfumes.com — CHF 117–205 (~$145–195)/50ml; US retail via Luckyscent, Twisted Lily

recommendations.name: Incense Rosé
recommendations.notes: frankincense, myrrh, rose, spices, woods
recommendations.profileNote: Incense Extrême with rose laid over it. Tauer builds on his ambreine base — same class of high-dose amber that has given you headaches, so sample first.
recommendations.where: tauerperfumes.com — CHF 117–205 (~$145–195)/50ml; US retail via Luckyscent, Twisted Lily

recommendations.name: Vanilla Absolue
recommendations.notes: vanilla absolute, amber, dry woods
recommendations.profileNote: 2025 release and a candidate for the non-sweet vanilla slot — Tauer's vanillas run dry and ambery rather than gourmand. Tauer builds on his ambreine base — same class of high-dose amber that has given you headaches, so sample first.
recommendations.where: tauerperfumes.com — CHF 117–205 (~$145–195)/50ml; US retail via Luckyscent, Twisted Lily

recommendations.name: L'Air des Alpes Suisses
recommendations.notes: fir balsam, alpine herbs, woods, resins
recommendations.profileNote: Tauer's alpine green. Less photorealistic than Pineward but better constructed. Tauer builds on his ambreine base — same class of high-dose amber that has given you headaches, so sample first.
recommendations.where: tauerperfumes.com — CHF 117–205 (~$145–195)/50ml; US retail via Luckyscent, Twisted Lily

recommendations.name: Mecca Balsam
recommendations.notes: frankincense, myrrh, labdanum, balsams, benzoin
recommendations.profileNote: Balsamic incense, 100% natural, 33ml for €55. Cheapest serious all-natural route into incense and myrrh anywhere.

recommendations.name: Oak Moss
recommendations.notes: oakmoss, green notes, woods
recommendations.profileNote: Natural oakmoss soliflore-style study at €29. A reference material more than a composition.

recommendations.name: Ihram
recommendations.notes: frankincense, sandalwood, musk
recommendations.profileNote: Clean frankincense and sandalwood. The quiet, devotional end of the incense range.

recommendations.name: Ummagumma Extra
recommendations.notes: incense, dark chocolate, woods
recommendations.profileNote: Incense against dark chocolate. Fazzolari is a painter first and the compositions are odd in a good way.
recommendations.where: fzotic.com — from $58 (house rebranded from Bruno Fazzolari)

recommendations.name: Vetiverissimo
recommendations.notes: vetiver, cedar, modern spice
recommendations.profileNote: Clean modern vetiver at $58. Cheap enough to be a low-risk test of the house.
recommendations.where: fzotic.com — from $58 (house rebranded from Bruno Fazzolari)

recommendations.name: Ghost Pine
recommendations.notes: pine needles, resin-streaked bark, cold mountain air, leaf litter, twisted roots, wet mossy earth
recommendations.profileNote: The cheapest photorealistic boreal green you will find, at $103 with $9 samples. Resin and wet earth rather than air-freshener pine.

recommendations.name: Vanilla Smoke
recommendations.notes: Madagascar vanilla absolute, tea smoked over pine, Siam wood, saffron, ambergris
recommendations.profileNote: Non-sweet vanilla and tea in the same bottle — the best version of that combination for your profile. $220/30ml is over band; the $8 sample is not.

recommendations.name: Fig
recommendations.notes: fig sap, fig leaves, rose, Atlas cedarwood, black pepper, frankincense
recommendations.profileNote: Fig over frankincense — the only thing found that serves two of your six profiles at once. $240 is over band; the 100ml refill is better per ml.

recommendations.name: Premier Figuier
recommendations.notes: fig leaf, fig milk, green almond, coconut, sandalwood
recommendations.profileNote: Giacobetti's other fig and the one remaining fig benchmark worth owning alongside Philosykos. Indie has no real answer to it under $200.

recommendations.name: Wildly Fig
recommendations.notes: fig, green notes, woods
recommendations.profileNote: New 2026 fig release. Price not verified against the house's own site — sample before trusting it.

recommendations.name: Fig Infusion
recommendations.notes: fig, mandarin, clementine, freesia, orange blossom, Sri Lankan black tea, cedarwood, sandalwood, benzoin
recommendations.profileNote: RULED OUT. In band at €94/100ml and fig plus black tea on paper, but orange blossom sits in the heart and that has read as urine on you. Also commonly miscredited to Giacobetti — it is Nathalie Lorson.

recommendations.name: Lust in Paradise
recommendations.notes: pink pepper, peony, litchi, Petalia, musk, white cedar extract, amber
recommendations.profileNote: RULED OUT. Three separate conflicts: litchi is built on the same sulfurous fruity family as blackcurrant and buchu, which turn sour on you, and reviewers independently report a sour drydown; Petalia is a synthetic peony captive that one reviewer reads as cat pee, the same failure mode as orange blossom and tuberose; and the white-musk-plus-amber base is the high-dose synthetic amber that triggers headaches. Also $265/50ml, over band, from a fast-release house.
